video.title: I Tried the Costco Gold Hack (How Much I Actually Made)

summary: Chris Koerner tests buying a 1 oz gold bar at Costco and describes a CollectPure workflow for selling bullion online. Local buyers offer less than his $4,209 purchase price, so the proposed profit depends on a better online resale price and stacked card rewards. At the end of the video, the bar has been shipped and he is waiting to be paid; no completed sale or realized profit is shown. The video also mentions buyers who use gold bars to make jewelry, sometimes outsourcing manufacture overseas.

ideas.name: Buy Costco gold bars and resell them online

ideas.business_model: Buy physical gold at retail and resell it through a marketplace; the host also describes credit-card and Costco rewards as part of the potential margin.

pricing.model: Buy at Costco's retail price and resell through an online marketplace at a price intended to beat local buy offers.

pricing.notes: The marketplace sale price and marketplace fees are not confirmed. The host describes potential cashback rewards separately; actual reward eligibility depends on the card and how Costco categorizes the purchase.

acquisition_channels.details: The host lists the gold bar on CollectPure, a precious-metals marketplace where another individual buys it. CollectPure is described as handling authentication and escrow.

quote.text: So, I list it for sale on CollectPure. Once it sells, they send me a shipping label, and I go to FedEx, as you see here.

acquisition_channels.details: The host phones local gold buyers to request quotes; he does not sell to them because their bids are below his target. He also phones Costco to check stock. These calls are to businesses, not prospective individual customers.

ideas.delivery: The seller buys and physically handles the gold, lists it, triple-packs it, takes photos and keeps receipts, then drops it at FedEx using the marketplace label. CollectPure receives and tests the bar, repacks it, pays the seller and ships it to the buyer. The host says the test bar was shipped and he was waiting for payment.
unit_economics_claims: The host opens with a second-hand claim of $2,000–$20,000 weekly profit; the video does not substantiate it with completed sales or accounts (metric_claims item 2).
The test bar cost $4,209, while the intended resale price was about $4,150–$4,160; local offers were lower (metric_claims items 14–18).
The host estimates that card and Costco rewards could offset the resale discount, but the rewards and net return are not verified in the video (metric_claims items 23–30).
Shipping overnight was estimated at $30; CollectPure's fee and the actual shipping cost are not stated (metric_claims item 21).
ideas.startup_cost: The test bar cost $4,209; other startup costs are not stated.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated; at the end of the video the bar had been shipped and the host was waiting to be paid.

acquisition.how: A marketplace listing can attract buyers, but checking stock, obtaining the bar and comparing local offers involve manual calls and a physical purchase.

onboarding.how: An online marketplace can handle account setup and listing workflows, but a person must provide the bar details and create or review the listing.

delivery.how: A person must obtain, handle, package and physically ship the gold bar.

billing.how: Marketplace escrow and payout can automate payment steps, while card selection, reward tracking and reconciling a high-value transaction need human checks.

support.how: The marketplace performs authentication, but a seller may need to handle shipping questions, payment delays or buyer disputes.

uk_applicability.notes: The buy-and-resell model could transfer, but the video depends on US Costco pricing and card rewards, Venmo, CollectPure and local buyer quotes. A UK version would need equivalent bullion stock, a suitable marketplace and locally available rewards; check UK tax and product rules.

risks: The host does not show a completed sale or disclose realized profit; the opening weekly profit range is not substantiated in the demonstration.
The local quotes are below the $4,209 purchase price, so the host depends on an unconfirmed online sale price and reward eligibility.
Gold prices can move between purchase, listing and sale, changing the spread.
The transcript does not state CollectPure's fees, payout timing, shipping insurance cost or the actual reward payout.
The transaction ties up substantial cash in physical inventory and requires secure packaging and shipping.
The host says card cashback can depend on whether Costco is categorized as a grocery purchase, and that not all cards categorize it that way.
